raw_response:
I need to think about this year carefully. I'm 75 now, been farming these 5.2 mu for 55 years. My wife and I, just the two of us now. The children are working in the city, sending some money but not much. We need this land to feed ourselves and have a little cash for medicine and other expenses.

**Winter wheat — planting now**

It's early October. The soil is still warm enough. I've been growing wheat on all 5.2 mu since I was 20. I know every corner of these fields. Last year the wheat did alright — I got about 420 kg per mu. The year before was better, nearly 480, but last spring was dry and I had to pump more water than I wanted. Water costs keep going up.

For seed, I'll use the improved variety I've been using for the past few years. I save some seed but I also buy fresh seed every couple of years to keep the vigor up. This year I'm buying fresh seed — about 12.5 kg per mu. Costs around 45 yuan per mu. I know some farmers are trying new hybrid seeds but at my age I don't want surprises. What I know works.

For fertilizer, the extension technician told me I should do soil testing and calculate precise rates. I listen to him, he's a good young man. But I've been putting down roughly the same amount for decades and it works. I'll use about 16 kg of nitrogen per mu total, split into two applications. Base fertilizer before planting: about 10 kg of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) and some urea. Then at jointing stage in spring, if the wheat looks yellow, I'll topdress with another 6-8 kg of urea. Last year I topdressed a bit late and the wheat was already heading, so I wasted some money. This year I'll watch closer. I'll put about 5 kg of phosphorus and 4 kg of potassium per mu in the base dressing. I buy the compound fertilizer because it's convenient — one bag covers everything.

Irrigation — I'll irrigate 3 times for sure. First, right after planting to help germination. Second at jointing in March or April, depending on rain. Third at grain filling in May. If it's very dry like two years ago, maybe a fourth time at booting, but pumping water costs 25-30 yuan each time for electricity. Three times should be enough if winter snow is decent. Total about 3 times, maybe 4 if drought.

Pesticide — I'll spray herbicide once in early spring for weeds. The broadleaf weeds always come up. That's about 15 yuan per mu. For insects, I don't spray unless I see aphids or something. At my age I can walk the field and see. Fungicide? Only if it looks bad, which it rarely does.

Tillage — I'll till once lightly with the small rotary tiller I have. My neighbor has a tractor and sometimes helps, but I can manage with my own machine. At my age, the vibration hurts my hands but it's only 5 mu, I can do it in two days.

Labor — Planting wheat takes my wife and me about 4 days total. She helps with broadcasting fertilizer and seed. Harvest will need hired help — I can't carry wheat bundles anymore. I'll hire two workers for 2 days at harvest, that's about 200 yuan total. For the rest, family labor: about 12 family days across the season for wheat.

I expect about 400-450 kg per mu this year. I'm hoping for 450 but planning for 400. Last year was 420, and the weather has been strange. Better to be conservative.

**Summer maize — planning ahead**

The wheat comes off in early June. I need to get the maize in within a week, sometimes less. That's the busy time. I'll plant maize on all 5.2 mu again.

Seed: hybrid maize seed. I buy fresh every year — you can't save hybrid seed, everyone knows that. About 2.5 kg per mu, costs about 55 yuan per mu. I use the same variety as last year, the one my nephew recommended. Good yield, about 500 kg per mu if the rain comes.

Fertilizer for maize: I put all of it at planting or shortly after. No time for fancy split applications in summer — the crop grows so fast and I'm busy. About 14 kg nitrogen per mu, 4 kg phosphorus, 3 kg potassium. I use compound fertilizer plus some urea. Total fertilizer cost around 130 yuan per mu for both crops together, roughly.

Irrigation for maize: Depends entirely on rain. If July and August are normal, maybe 1-2 irrigations. If drought, 3 times. But pumping in summer is expensive and the water table is dropping. I'll say 2 times on average — once at jointing, once at filling. But honestly, I might only do once if it rains. Let's plan for 2.

Pesticide for maize: Herbicide at planting, maybe one insecticide if the corn borers show up. I usually spray herbicide, that's it unless there's a visible problem.

Labor for maize: Planting is quick — 2 days with my wife. Harvest in late September, I'll hire help again. Maybe 2 workers for 2 days, 200 yuan. Family labor about 8 days across the season.

Yield expectation: 450-500 kg per mu. I'll plan for 450 to be safe. Two years ago I got 520, but that was exceptional.

**Money matters**

Total input costs: seed (wheat 45 + maize 55 = 100), fertilizer for both crops about 140 per mu, pesticides maybe 30, irrigation electricity about 80, hired labor 400. That's about 350 yuan per mu times 5.2 mu = roughly 1,820 yuan total. That's a lot for me. I have about 2,500 yuan cash set aside for farming this year. The rest is for emergencies. I can't spend more.

I thought about putting more fertilizer — the extension guy says 20 kg N per mu for wheat would give higher yield. But that's another 20 kg of urea, about 60 yuan more, and what if the weather is bad? Then I wasted the money. Better to stick with what I know. I'm 75. I don't need to gamble.

One thing — my back is getting worse. My wife is 73. We can't work like we used to. If hired labor gets more expensive or if I'm too sick, we might have to give some land to my nephew. But not yet. One more year.
